v7 (3 ep + LR 3e-5) regressed by -0.005 (last) / -0.002 (mean) relative to v6. Likely reasons:

3 epochs overfits the LM objective and the geometric task is forgotten

H-4’ FAIL — at 7B scale, geometric regularization with cross-sentence InfoNCE + margin push has reached the ceiling of marginal improvement (~+0.03 in best Δ, threshold +0.05). The trend is real and consistent (λ↑ margin↑, last > mean), but the magnitude is too small.




A: Accept 7B H-4’ FAIL — close Phase 2 7B side, write summary report
B: Try a different loss design — hard negative mining, SupCon with explicit margin, or reweight the margin-push coefficient
C: Expand paraphrase corpus (50 → 100 concepts) to give the geometric loss more signal
D: Change pooling strategy — attention-pooled, CLS token, or last-3-token average

title: About
text:
Geometry of Meaning is a research project exploring whether explicit geometric regularisation of hidden states — pulling together paraphrases of the same concept, pushing apart different concepts — can improve a language model’s representation geometry, as measured by a concept-grouped margin metric.


Standard language-model fine-tuning is augmented with a small auxiliary loss:
\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{aux}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{InfoNCE}} + 0.1 \cdot \text{ReLU}(\cos_{\text{neg}} - 0.5)
\]
where \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{InfoNCE}}\) is a temperature-scaled cross-entropy over paraphrase pairs in a small micro-batch, and the margin term explicitly penalises inter-cluster cosines above 0.5.




Model: Qwen2.5 family (0.5B + 7B)
Adaptation: LoRA (0.5B) / QLoRA 4-bit nf4 (7B)
Hardware: Apple Silicon MPS (0.5B), Kaggle T4 16GB (7B)
Loss: PEFT + custom cross-sentence InfoNCE
Reporting: Quarto + gh-pages





GitHub: https://github.com/math4mad/Geometry-Of-Meaning
Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/code/math4amd/geometry-meaning-7b-georeg

Phase 1 已用 Qwen2.5-{0.5B, 7B}-Instruct 提取 50 概念 × 4 变体 = 200 改写语料的内部表征， 发现 7B 在 last_token 池上比 0.5B 出现更明显的概念内聚性（参 0.5B vs 7B 报告）。

title: 0.5B v1-v3 — Cross-Sentence InfoNCE
text:
All 0.5B experiments use Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct + LoRA (r=16, α=32), MPS (Apple Silicon), 2 epochs, 50 paraphrase concepts × 5 paraphrases.


Loss design: for each sentence, take the last-layer hidden state, divide into two halves along the sequence axis, and apply InfoNCE between the two halves.
Why it failed: the proxy optimises token-level smoothness within one sentence, not cross-sentence concept alignment. The geometric loss did decrease (0.55 → 0.49), but the concept margin collapsed:

title: Geometry of Meaning
text:
Phase 2 explores whether cross-sentence geometric regularization — pulling together hidden states of paraphrases belonging to the same concept while pushing apart different concepts — can measurably improve the concept-grouped margin in a language model’s last-token / mean-pool representation space.


For a paraphrase corpus where every concept \(c\) has \(n_c\) paraphrases \(\{s_{c,1}, \ldots, s_{c,n_c}\}\), a small geometric loss
\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{geo}} = \sum_c \sum_{i,j \in \text{pos}(c)} \log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(h_i, h_j)/\tau)}{\sum_{k \neq i} \exp(\text{sim}(h_i, h_k)/\tau)}
\]
added to the standard LM loss should make the model’s hidden states of paraphrases cluster by concept.
The primary metric is concept-grouped margin:
\[
M = \frac{1}{N_c}\sum_c \frac{1}{n_c^2}\sum_{i,j} \cos(h_{c,i}, h_{c,j}) - \frac{1}{N_c(N_c-1)}\sum_{c\neq c'}\frac{1}{n_c n_{c'}}\sum_{i,j}\cos(h_{c,i}, h_{c',j})
\]
H-4 is PASS when \(M(\text{trained}) - M(\text{baseline}) \geq 0.05\).

title: Phase 2 Overview
text:
We start from a paraphrase corpus of 50 concepts with 5 paraphrases per concept, totalling 250 sentences. Each sentence expresses the same concept in different surface forms:
Concept 0:
  - "the cat sat on the mat"
  - "a feline was resting on the rug"
  - "the kitten lounged on the carpet"
  - ...

Concept 1:
  - "she wrote a letter to her friend"
  - "the woman composed a note for her pal"
  - ...
We extract hidden states from a language model, then compute:

intra-cluster cosine — average \(\cos(h_{c,i}, h_{c,j})\) over paraphrase pairs of the same concept
inter-cluster cosine — average \(\cos(h_{c,i}, h_{c',j})\) over paraphrase pairs of different concepts
margin = intra − inter (a larger margin ⇒ better concept clustering)




We add a cross-sentence InfoNCE loss computed on a micro-batch of \(M\) sentences drawn from \(K\) concepts:
\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{InfoNCE}} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{i=1}^{M} -\log \frac{\sum_{j \in \text{pos}(i)} \exp(\text{sim}(z_i, z_j)/\tau)}{\sum_{k \neq i} \exp(\text{sim}(z_i, z_k)/\tau)}
\]
where \(\text{pos}(i)\) are the indices of sentences sharing the same concept as sentence \(i\), and \(z_i\) is either the last-token or mean-pool hidden state of the final non-pad position.
We pair this with a margin-push auxiliary that explicitly penalises inter-cluster cosines above 0.5:
\[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{margin}} = \text{ReLU}(\cos_{\text{neg}} - 0.5)
\]
Total loss:
\[
\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{LM}} + \lambda \cdot (\mathcal{L}_{\text{InfoNCE}} + 0.1 \cdot \mathcal{L}_{\text{margin}})
\]




v1 (block-internal) computed InfoNCE over positions within the same sentence’s hidden states. This optimised local token-level smoothness, not cross-sentence concept alignment. Result: H-4 FAIL.
v2 (micro-batch only) broke the LM training distribution by replacing LM batches with paraphrase-only micro-batches. LM loss exploded to 6.85, InfoNCE = NaN. Result: H-4 FAIL.
v3 (LM stream + periodic micro-batch) keeps the standard LM training distribution (stream block of 128 tokens), and every \(G\) steps pauses to do one micro-batch of \(M\) paraphrases for \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{InfoNCE}}\). The LM flow stays stable; geometric loss is auxiliary. Result: H-4 PASS on 0.5B.
